items.title: Palitronica Closes Series A Funding Led by BDC, with Three Kings Capital, Frostbite, and Unpopular Funds

items.title: Palitronica Supports Bell’s MV-75 Cheyenne Program with Cyber Assurance for Electronic Components
items.summary: Palitronica announced its work with Bell Textron Inc. to provide state-of-the-art cyber assurance to critical electronics for the Bell MV-75 Cheyenne II, formerly known as the U.S. Army’s Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA) program.

items.title: Why Invalid Commands Are Useful Evidence in Firmware Testing
items.summary: Invalid commands can reveal what firmware does beyond its visible response. Learn how PowerFuzzer uses command-response-power evidence to detect hidden commands, firmware drift, undocumented functionality, and potential backdoors in black-box embedded systems.

items.title: AI-Powered Firmware Assessment Without Source Code
items.summary: By combining AI-powered fuzzing with power side-channel analysis, PowerFuzzer detects undocumented functionality, hidden behaviour, firmware changes, and potential backdoors without requiring source code access. It supports the assessment of embedded systems across aerospace, automotive, industrial, security, networking, and critical infrastructure applications.

items.title: Dual-Use Technology Is Reshaping Defence Procurement: What That Means for Electronics Assurance.
items.summary: Defence organizations are turning to commercial innovation not simply because it is less expensive, but because it offers access to the speed, scale, and technological agility required to maintain operational advantage in an increasingly dynamic security environment. But the same supply chains that enable rapid innovation also create new vulnerabilities.

items.title: Webcast: The Technology Behind PowerFuzzer | AI-Powered Firmware Validation and Side-Channel Analysis
items.summary: In this webcast, Sebastian Fischmeister explains the technology behind PowerFuzzer and how it combines AI-powered fuzzing with power side-channel analysis to assess firmware without requiring source code access.

items.title: Scaling Drone Manufacturing Without Losing Control
items.summary: The rapid expansion of autonomous systems is often framed as a question of scale. Production volumes are increasing, deployment scenarios are diversifying, and demand across defence, infrastructure, and commercial sectors continues to accelerate. For manufacturers, however, the more consequential shift is not scale itself, but how these systems are being built.

items.title: Poster: Thermal Compensation in RF Measurement Electronics Attestation Systems
items.summary: Presented at IPC Apex 2026, our poster offers a practical step toward deploying physics-based, black-box verification methods in production, not just controlled lab settings.

items.title: On-demand Webinar: The Hidden Risk That Can Crash Your Drone Manufacturing
items.summary: In this webinar, join Sebastian Fischmeister, pioneer in electronics integrity defense, and Seth Lloyd, Defense contractor advisor and U.S. Naval aviator, as they discuss the risks associated with COTS drones, and explore ways to secure rapid-delivery manufacturing.

items.title: Sovereign Sustainability and Government Responsibility: Why Verification Matters More Than Ownership
items.summary: Modern government electronics supply chains are global by necessity. Semiconductors, printed circuit boards, subassemblies, firmware, and final system integration routinely cross multiple borders and involve layers of suppliers that are difficult to fully map or control. While domestic manufacturing capacity remains strategically important, no government can realistically own or internalize every element of the electronics supply chain without unacceptable cost, delay, or capability gaps.

items.title: Understanding Sovereign Sustainability in Electronics Supply Chains
items.summary: Sovereign sustainability for critical infrastructure refers to a country’s ability to design, operate, maintain, and renew essential systems over the long term without losing control to external actors. Critical infrastructure is sovereignly sustainable when a state can keep essential services running during crises such as war, trade disruption, cyber incidents, or climate shocks, using domestic capabilities and trusted partners, without being exposed to coercion or sudden system failure.

items.title: Physics-Based Electronics Verification
items.summary: Anvil Checkpoint is a non-destructive electronics verification platform that detects internal differences in electronic hardware early, efficiently, and without assumptions. Using physics-based RF measurements and AI, Anvil establishes a known-good signature of a device and flags any deviation, even when designs, documentation, or firmware are unavailable.

items.title: Manufacturing-Grade Electronics Quality and Supplier Assurance
items.summary: Manufacturers face increasing risk from hidden defects, undocumented substitutions, and supplier process drift. Anvil Checkpoint addresses these challenges using physics-based RF measurements combined with AI, accessed through standard ports.

items.title: Hardware and Software Validation for Scaleable sUAS Production
items.summary: Silent supplier changes, hidden defects, and undocumented software drift are some of the biggest causes of field failures and RMAs in scaled drone programs. The Anvil Checkpoint gives drone manufacturers an objective way to verify whether received COTS electronics are truly equivalent to what was previously qualified.

items.title: Canadian Approach to Supply Chain Cybersecurity in the Electronics Sector
items.summary: Supply chain attacks are increasing across the global electronics industry. Palitronica, a Canadian technology company born from research at the University of Waterloo, is responding with a focused innovation strategy aimed at protecting critical sectors such as automotive, aerospace, and defence.

items.summary: We’re honoured to receive first place in the Cluster Inspection & Quality category. This recognition reflects our drive to push the boundaries of hardware cybersecurity and manufacturing integrity.

items.title: How to Achieve Physics-Powered Assurance with Zero Risk to Your Electronics Hardware
items.summary: Anvil Checkpoint uses a non-invasive method to verify the integrity of electronic devices. By injecting a low-power RF signal into the target and analyzing the reflections.

items.title: Webcast: The Physics Powering Anvil CheckPoint Technology
items.summary: In this presentation, Co-Founder and CTO Carlos Moreno explains the physics behind the technology—likening it to “shouting into a cave and listening to the echo”.

items.title: Protect Your Business: Catch Compliance & Hardware Config Issues with Incoming Inspection
items.summary: Counterfeit and misconfigured electronics slip past visual inspections every day, putting safety, compliance, and your reputation at risk. Learn why traditional incoming inspection isn’t enough and how to deliver fast, non-invasive verification that meets NIST 800-53 and 800-161 standards.

Read about the findings in the eBook: Broad-Spectrum Testing of Electronic Control Units.
